List has been revised.

2. Heard Shri Sharad Kumar Srivastava, learned counsel for the applicant as well as Shri R.P. Patel,
learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

3 . Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No.98 of 2023, under Sections 452, 354, 506, 376, 323 I.P.C.,
Police Station Bilsi, District Budaun, during the pendency of trial.

4. As per the allegations in the FIR, the applicant is stated to have barged into the house of the informant on 24.2.2023 at about 06:00 a.m. and is stated to have outraged her modesty by showing country made pistol to her.

The FIR was instituted on 3.3.2023 at about 05:20 p.m. under Sections Sudhir vs State Of U.P. on 18 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103961301/
1 452, 354, 506 I.P.C.
5.

entities.text: Sections Sudhir vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PROVISION

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that he is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
The victim herein is 40 years of age and she is a married lady.
There are no allegations of rape leveled in the FIR.
The FIR itself is delayed by about seven days and there is no explanation of the said delay caused.
Later on, during the statement of the victim recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C., the allegations of rape have been added.
The said story has been added after legal consultation.
Learned counsel has stated that the victim has wrongly mentioned her age to be 25 years.
Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
There is no criminal history of the applicant.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 7.4.2023.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.
6. Per contra, learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the bail application on the ground that there is a contusion in the thigh of the victim.
7. In rebuttal, learned counsel for the applicant has stated that the said medical examination has been conducted belatedly and no duration has been mentioned in it.

8. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

9. Let the applicant- Sudhir involved in aforementioned case crime number be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two heavy sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
(i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence during the trial.
(ii). The applicant will not pressurize/ intimidate the prosecution witness.
(iii) The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.
(iv) The applicant shall not commit an offence similar to the offence of which he is accused, or suspected of the commission of which he is suspected.

(v) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.

Sudhir vs State Of U.P. on 18 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103961301/
2 10.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
Identity, status and residence proof of the applicant and sureties be verified by the court concerned before the bonds are accepted.

11. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
[Krishan Pahal, J.]
Order Date :- 18.5.2023
